title: 2014 HMMT February Geometry Problem 4
statement:
In quadrilateral \(A B C D, \angle D A C=98^{\circ}, \angle D B C=82^{\circ}, \angle B C D=70^{\circ}\), and \(B C=A D\). Find \(\angle A C D\).

[Diagram omitted from this imported transcription; consult the HMMT archive while reviewing the problem.]

solutions.text: 28 Let \(B^{\prime}\) be the reflection of \(B\) across \(C D\). Note that \(A D=B C\), and \(\angle D A C+\angle C B^{\prime} D=\) \(180^{\circ}\), so \(A C B^{\prime} D\) is a cyclic trapezoid. Thus, \(A C B^{\prime} D\) is an isosceles trapezoid, so \(\angle A C B^{\prime}=98^{\circ}\). Note that \(\angle D C B^{\prime}=\angle B C D=70^{\circ}\), so \(\angle A C D=\angle A C B^{\prime}-\angle D C B^{\prime}=98^{\circ}-70^{\circ}=28^{\circ}\).
